questions.text:
Looking at the surface of a smooth 3-dimensional object from the outside, which
one of the following options is TRUE?
questions.solution:
A smooth 3D object (e.g. a peanut or a bowl-shaped surface) can bulge outward in some places and curve inward in others. Nothing forces it to be convex or concave everywhere, and "smooth" rules out edges.

Answer: The surface may be concave in some places and convex in other places

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: The surface of the object must be concave everywhere.
The surface of the object must be convex everywhere.
The surface of the object may be concave in some places and convex in other places.
The object can have edges, but no corners.

questions.text:
A survey for a certain year found that 90% of pregnant women received medical care at least once before giving birth. Of these women, 60% received medical care from doctors, while 40% received medical care from other healthcare providers.
Given this information, which one of the following statements can be inferred with certainty?
questions.solution:
Women who received care from doctors = 60% of 90% = 54% of all pregnant women.

54% is more than half, so more than half received care at least once from a doctor. The data says nothing about "at most once".

Answer: More than half of the pregnant women received medical care at least once from a doctor

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options:
More than half of the pregnant women received medical care at least once from a
doctor.

Less than half of the pregnant women received medical care at least once from a
doctor.

More than half of the pregnant women received medical care at most once from a
doctor.

Less than half of the pregnant women received medical care at most once from a
doctor.

questions.text:
A series of natural numbers [latex]F_1,F_2,F_3,F_4,F_5,F_6,F_7,... [/latex] obeys [latex]F_{n+1}=F_n+F_{n-1} [/latex] for all integers [latex]n \geq 2[/latex].
If [latex]F_6=37[/latex], and [latex]F_7=60[/latex], then what is [latex]F_1[/latex]?
questions.solution:
Work backwards using [latex]F_{n-1}=F_{n+1}-F_n[/latex]:
- [latex]F_5=60-37=23[/latex]
- [latex]F_4=37-23=14[/latex]
- [latex]F_3=23-14=9[/latex]
- [latex]F_2=14-9=5[/latex]
- [latex]F_1=9-5=4[/latex]

Answer: 4

questions.text: We reached the station late, and _______ missed the train.
questions.solution:
"Nearly missed the train" means almost missed it (but caught it). Near is not an adverb here, and "utterly / mostly missed" do not make sense.

Answer: nearly
